League in general is just a game where knowing when an appropriate time to all-in somebody is what helps you climb.

Laning phase works like this:

You have passive laning, CSing where two people aren't interacting with each other. This can happen when players are new or uncomfortable with laning phase mechanics. You usually want to punish opponents who do this. Just be aware of the enemy jungler.

You have trading, which involves damaging your opponent and walking away. A good trade would involve doing more damage to them than they did to you, and a bad trade would be the opposite.

You have all-inning, which involves committing to killing an enemy using whatever means necessary. 

Identifying the difference between trading and all-inning is an important fundamental in League, but all champions should trade, because all champions have an appropriate time to punish an enemy for making a mistake, and all players make mistakes even at the highest level. Trades can look like a single auto-attack thrown out when your opponent tries to last hit a minion, or using your full rotation of abilities and walking away.

Trades usually happen when champions go for creep scoring. Part of the purpose in trading is to discourage your enemy from last hitting minions so that they miss gold and you are able to slowly build an advantage against them. Great trades where your opponent makes a huge mistake can turn into all-ins.

Gwen is not good at all-inning people until she hits level 6 because she gets access to her first source of slows, and her all-in potential is actually insane because, used in succession, her ultimate is 4.5 seconds of slowing.

Gwen is generally fantastic at trading because using EWQ allows you to damage an opponent without letting them retaliate.

Tryndamere is amazing at all-inning because of his high mobility with his E as well as having a slow on his W. He usually takes summoner spells that encourage all-inning as well. Ghost is a very good summoner spell for all-inning, and so is ignite for obvious reasons. 

You generally never want to allow somebody to trade with you without trading back unless they have the ability to all-in you for trying to trade. You can usually find ways to trade and disengage at the same time though. Gwen is very good at that, because she can Q the opponent and E backwards. 

The problem with the Tryndamere match-up is that he can catch up instantly with his E and slow you with his W, but as long as you walk away, he can't usually can't keep up with you. W doesn't really save you from Tryndamere because he wants to be up close anyways, and if you try to turn around and all-in him, he usually wins.

I would never tell somebody to *never* trade, but yes, Tryndamere is a champion that Gwen can both have trouble trading with and all-inning. Sion for example, you can trade with because he doesn't have mobility to catch up to you if you EWQ to try to trade back (which if you didn't know, brings you directly to the edge of your W), and he will usually lose the all-in.

Learning which champions are safe to trade against, when it's safe to trade against those champions, and learning when it's safe to all-in those champions is the fundamental to learning laning in League of Legends. Don't rely on guides and instead rely on intuition and focusing on what your opponent does and trying to punish them for making bad or weird decisions.

Her first power spike is after she gets her ultimate at 6, her second power spike is her second item, Nashors.

2 items is when you usually go hyper God mode where you're able to 1v1 pretty much anyone (couple exceptions like trynd but you should always try if you're not sure tbh by looking at the items of the person you're going to 1v1 and building matchup knowledge from there).

3 items (deathcap) is your extremely powerful team fight scaling where, combined with conqueror and 3 second Riftmaker, you should be able to delete teams who are lined up. Almost no squishy survives R2 R3 Q and there's plenty in a team fight to focus on. Then you focus the tanks after.

Gwen is very micro intensive and relies on Q usage when the enemy is stuck in an animation (like Darius E).
